body.en: When goods are sold on credit, the drawer debits the drawee and credits sales. On receiving the accepted bill, the drawer debits *Bills* Receivable Account and credits the drawee. The drawee mirrors this: he debits the drawer and credits Bills Payable Account. When the bill is met on the due date, the drawee debits Bills Payable and credits Bank.

points.en: Drawer: *Bills* Receivable A/c Dr, To Drawee A/c
Drawee: Drawer A/c Dr, To *Bills* Payable A/c
Drawee on payment: *Bills* Payable A/c Dr, To Bank A/c

title.en: Discounting a bill with the bank

caption.en: The drawer needs cash before the due date, so the bank buys the bill and keeps a discount: amount × rate × unexpired months ÷ 12.

body.en: If the drawer keeps the bill till maturity, she debits Bank and credits Bills Receivable when it is met. If she *discounts* it, the bank pays the amount less a discount: debit Bank and Discount on Bills, credit Bills Receivable. If she endorses it to her creditor, debit the creditor and credit Bills Receivable. If she sends it to the bank for collection, debit Bills Sent for Collection and credit Bills Receivable; when the bank collects it, debit Bank and credit Bills Sent for Collection. The drawee's entry on the due date is the same in every case.

points.en: *Discount* on bills is a loss (expense) for the drawer
The *drawee* always pays whoever holds the bill on the due date

Endorsement settles the drawer's own debt.

problem.en: On 1 May 2026 Kiran sold goods to Leela for ₹24,000 and drew a 3-month bill, which she accepted. On 4 June Kiran discounted it with his bank at 10% p.a. Pass the entry for discounting.

steps.en: The bill is due on 4 August (1 May + 3 months + 3 days).
From 4 June to 4 August is 2 months.
Entry: Bank A/c Dr ₹23,600; Discount on Bills A/c Dr ₹400; To Bills Receivable A/c ₹24,000.

answer.en: Bank ₹23,600 and Discount on Bills ₹400 debited; Bills Receivable ₹24,000 credited.

narration.en: Let us work this out step by step. On 1 May 2026 Kiran sold goods to Leela for ₹24,000 and drew a 3-month bill, which she accepted. On 4 June Kiran discounted it with his bank at 10% p.a. Pass the entry for discounting.

say.en: Let us work this out step by step. On 1 May 2026 Kiran sold goods to Leela for 24,000 rupees and drew a 3-month bill, which she accepted. On 4 June Kiran discounted it with his bank at 10 percent p.a. Pass the entry for discounting.
The bill is due on 4 August (1 May plus 3 months plus 3 days).
From 4 June to 4 August is 2 months.
Discount equals 24,000 times 10 over 100 times 2 over 12 equals 400 rupees.
Entry: Bank A over c Dr 23,600 rupees; Discount on Bills A over c Dr 400 rupees; To Bills Receivable A over c 24,000 rupees.
So the answer is Bank 23,600 rupees and Discount on Bills 400 rupees debited; Bills Receivable 24,000 rupees credited.

body.en: Whatever the drawer does with the bill (keep, discount, endorse, collect), the drawee passes the same two entries: accept the bill, then pay it.

points.en: The drawer debits Bills Receivable; the drawee credits Bills Payable.
Discounting brings cash early at the cost of a discount, a loss to the drawer.
Endorsement passes the bill to a creditor; collection leaves it with the bank till the due date.
The drawee records only the acceptance and the payment.
